Holly Trevino, a 26-year-old female, was initially diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia on September 6, 2018. She has been in remission since her initial treatment and has been under regular follow-up. Her last visit to the clinic was on June 2, 2025, for a routine check-up related to her leukemia status. During this visit, her blood pressure was recorded at 150/78 mmHg, and her weight was 225 pounds.

- Former smoker, 1 pack per day of cigarettes, quit on December 4, 2024.
- Consumes approximately 8 alcoholic drinks per week.
- No significant family history of medical conditions.

HOSPITAL COURSE:

She reported no acute complaints or symptoms suggestive of relapse. Physical examination was unremarkable, with stable vital signs and no evidence of infection or other complications. Her weight has fluctuated slightly over the years, with the highest recorded weight being 225 pounds on June 2, 2025, and the lowest being 212 pounds on October 23, 2022. Blood pressure readings have also been stable, ranging from 135/83 mmHg on February 12, 2024, to 150/78 mmHg on June 2, 2025.

She has had a few minor complaints over the years, including a rash noted on June 18, 2023, which resolved with conservative management. No other significant medical issues were reported during her follow-up visits.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Ms. Trevino is not currently on any medications for her leukemia, as she is in remission and under observation. She was advised to continue with her regular follow-up appointments and to maintain a healthy lifestyle.

FOLLOW-UP PLAN:
Ms. Trevino was discharged home in stable condition. She was advised to continue her regular follow-up appointments with the oncology clinic every six months to monitor her leukemia status. She was also encouraged to maintain a healthy lifestyle, including regular exercise and a balanced diet. Given her history of smoking, she was counseled on the importance of remaining smoke-free and the risks associated with alcohol consumption.
